event: EU ETS created for stationary installations (context; no aviation)
scope_change: Stationary installations only. Aviation not covered.
allocation_auction_share: At least 95% free in 2005-2007; at least 90% free in 2008-2012.
verbatim_quote: For the three-year period beginning 1 January 2005 Member States shall allocate at least 95 % of the allowances free of charge. For the five-year period beginning 1 January 2008, Member States shall allocate at least 90 % of the allowances free of charge.
notes: Entry-into-force article not re-read. Included because the EUA price series starts in 2005; Phase 1 (2005-2007) allowances could not be banked into Phase 2.

event: Aviation included in the EU ETS (full scope: all flights arriving at or departing from EU aerodromes)
date_applies_from: 2012-01-01 (surrender obligation); 2010 was the monitoring year for tonne-km benchmark data; transposition deadline 2010-02-02
scope_change: All flights arriving at or departing from an aerodrome in a Member State (intra-EU and extra-EU, both directions), with Annex I exemptions (e.g. de minimis operators).
cap_change: Total allowances for aircraft operators = 97% of historical aviation emissions in 2012 and 95% per year from 2013. Historical aviation emissions = mean of 2004, 2005 and 2006.
allocation_auction_share: 15% auctioned (2012 and from 2013); 3% special reserve (from 2013); remainder free by tonne-km benchmark. Commission FAQ on the EC aviation page states 82% free, 15% auctioned, 3% special reserve.
verbatim_quote: ‘From 1 January 2012 all flights which arrive at or depart from an aerodrome situated in the territory of a Member State to which the Treaty applies shall be included.’ | 1. For the period from 1 January 2012 to 31 December 2012, the total quantity of allowances to be allocated to aircraft operators shall be equivalent to 97 % of the historical aviation emissions. | 1. In the period referred to in Article 3c(1), 15 % of allowances shall be auctioned.
notes: Extended to EEA-EFTA states (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway) by EEA Joint Committee Decision 6/2011 of 1 April 2011 (per EC aviation page; that decision was not read). Third-country measures handled by new Article 25a.

event: EU-wide aviation cap, auction volume, special reserve and free allocation fixed for 2012 and 2013-2020
legal_act: Commission Decision 2011/389/EU (based on historical emissions set by Commission Decision 2011/149/EU)
cap_change: Union-wide historical aviation emissions 219,476,343 tCO2. Cap: 212,892,053 allowances for 2012; 208,502,526 per year from 2013.
verbatim_quote: 1. The Union-wide total number of allowances referred to in Article 3c(1) of Directive 2003/87/EC relating to the period from 1 January 2012 to 31 December 2012 is 212 892 053. 2. The Union-wide total number of allowances referred to in Article 3c(2) of Directive 2003/87/EC relating to each year of the period beginning on 1 January 2013 is 208 502 526.
quote_location: Article 1; recital 1 gives 219 476 343 tonnes of CO2
notes: These are EU-27 figures. EEA-wide quantities were set afterwards by EEA Joint Committee Decision 93/2011 (not read; numbers not recorded here).

event: Free-allocation benchmarks for aircraft operators
allocation_auction_share: Free allocation per operator = benchmark x verified 2010 tonne-km: 0.000679695907431681 allowances per tonne-km (2012); 0.000642186914222035 (2013-2020).
verbatim_quote: the benchmark to be used to allocate allowances free of charge to aircraft operators pursuant to Article 3e(1) of that Directive for the period from 1 January to 31 December 2012 shall be 0,000679695907431681 allowances per tonne-kilometre.
notes: Allocations based on 2010 tonne-km were to stay fixed until 2020 except where Article 25a acts require changes (recital 2).

event: Court of Justice upholds validity of the aviation inclusion (ATA v Secretary of State)
legal_act: CJEU Grand Chamber judgment, Case C-366/10
scope_change: No change; full scope confirmed as valid under the international law principles examined.
verbatim_quote: 2. Examination of Directive 2008/101 has disclosed no factor of such a kind as to affect its validity.
notes: Useful as an anticipation date for airlines and third countries just before obligations started.

event: Commission announces 'stop the clock' for extra-European flights
date_adopted: 2012-11-12 (announcement); 2012-11-20 (COM(2012) 697, date from EC aviation page document list)
scope_change: Proposed deferral of 2012 surrender and reporting obligations for flights into and out of Europe; intra-EU obligations unchanged.
verbatim_quote: 'Stopping the clock' on the implementation of the international aspects of aviation under the EU emissions trading system (EU ETS) means that the EU would not require allowances to be surrendered in April 2013 for emissions to and from the EU during 2012.
notes: Announcement date matters for anticipation: operators knew in November 2012 that extra-EU flights in calendar 2012 would not be enforced.

event: 'Stop the clock' decision: no enforcement for 2012 on flights to/from most non-EU countries
scope_change: Member States take no action for 2010-2012 reporting and 2012 surrender on flights to and from aerodromes in countries outside the Union that are not EFTA members, not EEA dependencies or territories and not acceding countries, provided operators did not receive or returned the corresponding 2012 free allowances. Flights within the EU and to/from EFTA states (including Switzerland) and acceding countries stayed covered for 2012.
cap_change: 2012 aviation allowances not issued or returned are cancelled.
allocation_auction_share: Auctioned 2012 aviation allowances reduced in proportion; any shortfall adjusted in 2013 auctions.
verbatim_quote: By way of derogation from Article 16 of Directive 2003/87/EC, Member States shall take no action against aircraft operators in respect of the requirements set out in Article 12(2a) and Article 14(3) of that Directive for the calendar years 2010, 2011 and 2012 in respect of activity to and from aerodromes in countries outside the Union that are not members of EFTA, dependencies and territories of States in the EEA or countries having signed a Treaty of Accession with the Union
notes: Retroactive: the full-scope obligation for 2012 was never enforced for most extra-EU routes. Treat 2012 as an intra-European treatment year with announcement in Nov 2012.

event: Scope limited to intra-EEA flights for 2013-2016
scope_change: Derogation for all emissions from flights to and from aerodromes in countries outside the EEA, and for flights between outermost regions and the rest of the EEA, in each year 2013-2016. 2013 intra-EEA reporting and surrender deadlines moved to 31 March 2015 and 30 April 2015. Non-commercial operators below 1,000 tCO2 per year excluded 2013-2020. Flights to countries that acceded in 2013 (Croatia) treated as intra-EEA.
cap_change: Allowances not allocated because of the derogation are cancelled.
allocation_auction_share: Free allowances reduced in proportion to the reduced surrender obligation; auctioned quantity reduced in proportion; auction share stays 15%.
verbatim_quote: (a) all emissions from flights to and from aerodromes located in countries outside the European Economic Area (EEA) in each calendar year from 1 January 2013 to 31 December 2016;
notes: Commission proposal COM(2013) 722 of 16 October 2013 had proposed a regional-airspace approach (per EC aviation page document list; not adopted in that form).

event: ICAO Assembly decides on CORSIA (global market-based measure from 2021)
legal_act: ICAO Assembly resolution adopted at the 39th Session (A39-3); current consolidated text A42-22
date_adopted: 2016-10 (month from EC aviation page; exact day not read)
scope_change: International flights between participating States; phased: pilot 2021-2023 and first phase 2024-2026 voluntary; second phase 2027-2035 mandatory for States above RTK thresholds, with exemptions (LDCs, SIDS, LLDCs).
cap_change: Offsetting of growth above baseline (see E15).
text_read_via: EC aviation page; ICAO A42-22 PDF (https://www.icao.int/sites/default/files/environmental-protection/Assembly42/Resolution-A42-22_CORSIA.pdf)
verbatim_quote: In October 2016, ICAO agreed on a Resolution for a global market-based measure to address CO 2 emissions from international aviation as of 2021. As a result, the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) was introduced.
notes: ICAO pages block automated download; A42-22 was read through a fetched copy of the PDF.

event: Intra-EEA scope extended to 2017-2023; linear reduction factor applied to aviation from 2021
scope_change: Derogation for flights to and from aerodromes outside the EEA (and outermost-region flights) extended to each calendar year 2013-2023, subject to review (Article 28b).
cap_change: From 2021 the number of allowances allocated to aircraft operators is subject to the linear reduction factor of Article 9 (2.2% from 2021 under Directive (EU) 2018/410).
allocation_auction_share: 15% auctioned retained; Commission to study cost pass-through with a view to increasing auctioning.
verbatim_quote: (a) all emissions from flights to and from aerodromes located in countries outside the EEA in each calendar year from 1 January 2013 to 31 December 2023, subject to the review referred to in Article 28b; | From 1 January 2021, the number of allowances allocated to aircraft operators shall be subject to the application of the linear factor referred to in Article 9, subject to the review referred to in Article 28b.
notes: Commission proposal COM(2017) 54 of 3 February 2017 (date from EC aviation page list).

event: Phase 4 reform: linear reduction factor 2.2% from 2021 (applies to aviation through E09)
verbatim_quote: ‘Starting in 2021, the linear factor shall be 2,2 %.’.
notes: General ETS reform; listed because Regulation 2017/2392 ties the aviation cap to this factor.

event: EU-Swiss ETS linking agreement enters into force
legal_act: Agreement between the EU and the Swiss Confederation on linking their ETSs (OJ L 322, 7.12.2017, p. 3); concluded by Council Decision (EU) 2018/219; Notice in OJ L 330, 20.12.2019
oj_publication: 2018-02-16 (Council Decision, OJ L 43, p. 1); 2019-12-20 (Notice, OJ L 330, p. 1)
scope_change: Swiss ETS covers aviation; flights from EEA to Switzerland covered by EU ETS; flights from Switzerland to EEA covered by Swiss ETS (see E12).
verbatim_quote: The Agreement between the European Union and the Swiss Confederation on the linking of their greenhouse gas emissions trading systems ( 1 ) enters into force on 1 January 2020, the procedure provided for in Article 21(4) of the Agreement having been completed on 6 December 2019.
quote_location: Notice concerning the entry into force
notes: Council Decision 2018/219 recital 4 says the Swiss ETS had to be extended to aviation before entry into force.

event: Incoming flights from Switzerland excluded from the EU ETS
scope_change: New Annex I point (l): flights from aerodromes in Switzerland to aerodromes in the EEA excluded from EU ETS.
allocation_auction_share: Free allocation adjusted by Commission Decision of 16 December 2020 on aviation allocation tables (per EC aviation page; not read).
verbatim_quote: ‘(l) flights from aerodromes situated in Switzerland to aerodromes situated in the EEA.’.

event: UK participation in the EU ETS ends with the Brexit transition period
date_applies_from: Transition period ends 2020-12-31; Union law (including the EU ETS) applied to the UK until then
scope_change: From 2021 UK aerodromes are outside the EEA for EU ETS purposes.
verbatim_quote: Article 126 Transition period There shall be a transition or implementation period, which shall start on the date of entry into force of this Agreement and end on 31 December 2020.
notes: Article 127 states Union law applies to and in the UK during the transition. EU ETS verified emissions file notes that GB-administered aircraft operator accounts are being migrated.

event: UK ETS starts, covering UK domestic flights and departing flights from the UK to the EEA
legal_act: The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Order 2020 (SI 2020/1265)
date_entry_into_force: Day after the day the Order is made, except as provided (Article 2)
scope_change: UK ETS aviation activity: flights departing UK aerodromes to the UK, the EEA, Gibraltar (and offshore structures), and flights arriving in the UK from Gibraltar. gov.uk now also lists flights departing the UK to Switzerland (amending instrument not identified).
allocation_auction_share: UK ETS Aviation Allocation Table for 2021-2025 (not read).
verbatim_quote: The UK Emissions Trading Scheme ( UK ETS ) came into effect on 1 January 2021.
quote_location: gov.uk 'Participating in the UK ETS', Overview; Order Schedule 1 para 1 for scope
notes: Northern Ireland electricity generators remain in the EU ETS (gov.uk); not relevant for aviation.

event: EU ETS covers EEA-to-UK flights; incoming UK-to-EEA flights excluded
scope_change: New Annex I point (m): flights from UK aerodromes to EEA aerodromes excluded from EU ETS. Under the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement, flights from the EEA to the UK are regulated under the EU ETS.
allocation_auction_share: Free allocation adjusted by a Commission Decision (OJ C 74, 2022, per EC aviation page; not read).
verbatim_quote: The Agreement provides that each party is to have in place an effective system of carbon pricing that covers aviation and that flights from aerodromes situated in the territory of the European Economic Area (EEA) to aerodromes situated in the United Kingdom are to be regulated under the EU ETS.
notes: So from 2021 London hubs face UK ETS on departures to the EEA and EU ETS on arrivals from the EEA.

event: CORSIA phases and baselines (pilot 2021-2023, first phase 2024-2026, second phase 2027-2035)
legal_act: ICAO Assembly Resolution A42-22 (consolidated statement, recalling the 39th Session decision); baseline change by the 41st Assembly
date_adopted: Baseline change: 2022-10-07 (41st Assembly, as stated in Directive (EU) 2023/958 recital); A42-22 adoption date not read
scope_change: Pilot and first phase: States that volunteered (88 States for 2021, 107 for 2022, 115 for 2023, 126 for 2024, 129 for 2025, 130 for 2026 per A42-22). Second phase: States above 0.5% of 2018 RTKs or within the top 90% cumulative RTKs, with exemptions.
cap_change: Sector growth factor uses 2019 emissions for 2021-2023 and 85% of 2019 emissions for 2024-2035.
verbatim_quote: a) Pilot phase applies from 2021 through 2023 to States that have volunteered to participate in the scheme. ... b) First phase applies from 2024 through 2026 to States that voluntarily participate in the pilot phase, as well as any other States that volunteer to participate in this phase ... e) Second phase applies from 2027 through 2035 to all States that have an individual share of international aviation activities in RTKs in year 2018 above 0.5 per cent of total RTKs
quote_location: A42-22 paragraph 9 (a page-number artifact between pages 3 and 4 removed); baseline in paragraph 11 b)
notes: EC aviation page: the 2019 baseline plus the rebound 'resulted in no offsetting obligations under CORSIA for aeroplane operators in 2021 and 2022'. EU position on voluntary participation from 1 January 2021: Council Decision (EU) 2020/954 of 25 June 2020 (listed on EC page; not read). Which non-EU hub States (Turkey, UAE, Qatar) volunteered for which years was not checked.

event: Aviation free allocation phased out; full auctioning from 2026; SAF allowances
date_entry_into_force: 2023-06-05 (20th day after OJ publication; also stated on EC aviation page)
scope_change: Flights departing the EEA to Switzerland and the UK added to the cap calculation from 2024 (they were not covered in 2023 for cap purposes).
cap_change: 2024 aviation cap = total 2023 allocation reduced by the linear reduction factor, increased for routes newly covered from 2024; linear factor 4.3% (2024-2027) and 4.4% (from 2028) under Directive (EU) 2023/959.
allocation_auction_share: 2024: 15% auctioned plus 25% of the remaining 85% (implied total 36.25%, computed). 2025: 15% plus 50% of the remaining 85% (implied 57.5%, computed). From 2026: all allowances that would have been free are auctioned. Free allowances in 2024-2025 distributed in proportion to 2023 verified emissions. Up to 20 million allowances reserved 2024-2030 for sustainable aviation fuel uptake.
verbatim_quote: ‘1. In the years 2024 and 2025, 15 % of the allowances referred to in Article 3c(5) and (7), as well as 25 % in 2024 and 50 % in 2025, respectively, of the remaining 85 % of those allowances, in respect of which free allocation would have taken place, shall be auctioned ... From 1 January 2026, the entire quantity of allowances in respect of which free allocation would have taken place in that year shall be auctioned
notes: EC aviation page summary: 'Free allocation to aircraft operators will be reduced by 25% in 2024 and by 50% 2025, moving to full auctioning for the sector by 2026.'

event: Intra-EEA (plus departures to UK and Switzerland) scope extended to end-2026; CORSIA applied to extra-EEA flights; 2026 review with possible extension to departing flights from 2027
date_applies_from: Derogation covers 2021-2026 emissions; Commission report due by 2026-07-01
scope_change: Derogation for flights to and from States outside the EEA (except flights to the UK or Switzerland) for 2021-2026. If the July 2026 report finds that the ICAO Assembly had not strengthened CORSIA by 31 December 2025, or that CORSIA States cover less than 70% of international aviation emissions, the accompanying proposal shall, as appropriate, apply the ETS to departing extra-EEA flights from January 2027 and exclude arriving flights.
allocation_auction_share: CORSIA: EU-based operators cancel units for 2021-2023 emissions by 31 January 2025 and for 2024-2026 by 31 January 2028.
verbatim_quote: all emissions from flights to and from aerodromes located in States outside the EEA, with the exception of flights to aerodromes located in the United Kingdom or Switzerland, in each calendar year from 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2026, subject to the review referred to in Article 28b;
notes: EC aviation page: 'The restriction of the geographical scope of the ETS is extended until the start of 2027.'

event: General ETS reform: linear reduction factor 4.3% (2024-2027) and 4.4% (from 2028)
cap_change: Union-wide quantity cut by 90 million allowances in 2024 and 27 million in 2026; linear factor 4.3% 2024-2027 and 4.4% from 2028. Aviation cap follows the linear factor via Article 3c(5) as amended by 2023/958.
verbatim_quote: The linear factor shall be 4,3 % from 2024 to 2027 and 4,4 % from 2028.

event: PROPOSAL (not adopted): ETS review would cover departing flights to non-EEA airports within 5,000 km of Frankfurt from 2029, citing hub leakage
date_applies_from: Proposed: derogation for extra-EEA flights continues 2027-2028; coverage of departing flights to aerodromes within 5,000 km of Frankfurt from 2029 to 2032, subject to a 2032 review
scope_change: Proposed new derogation keeps flights to aerodromes more than 5,000 km from Frankfurt outside the surrender obligation in 2029-2032; flights to closer non-EEA aerodromes would be covered (departing direction), with CORSIA cost deduction and an extension of CORSIA unit cancellation to 2035.
cap_change: Proposed commensurate increase in the cap.
verbatim_quote: This scope of application is around half the maximum distance of flights from the centre of Europe, taking account of analysis which indicates such routes are most susceptible to potential hub leakage. This coverage should apply from 2029 rather than 2027, for a period of four years and be dependent on the review in 2032.
quote_location: Proposal recital on Article 28a (recital numbered just before (83))
notes: Pending legislation; Council and Parliament positions not checked. Whether Istanbul and Gulf hubs fall inside 5,000 km of Frankfurt should be computed from airport coordinates before use.
